history.dynasty: Medieval origins; present structure attributed to the 19th century by the ruler of the Ranapur princely state (lightuptemples - verify). One travel source claims roots going back ~1,000 years.
history.period: Medieval (architectural dating uncertain); current temple 19th century per one source (verify). Conflicting dates across sources: Wikipedia infobox on a similarly-named page says 13th century, but that page appears to describe a different Bhubaneswar temple also called 'Ladu Baba' - treat dating with caution.
history.summary: The Ladubaba Temple at Sarankul (also spelled Sharanakul/Saranakul), Nayagarh district, Odisha, is one of the most important Shaivite shrines of southern Odisha. The presiding deity is Lord Shiva worshipped as Ladukeswar (Ladukesh Mahesh), affectionately called Ladu Baba - the name is said to come from the giant 'ladu' (sweet) offerings made to the deity. The temple shows a fusion of Kalinga and Dravidian temple architecture, and uniquely, prayers have traditionally been conducted by priests belonging to low castes. It is a rare shrine embodying the Hari-Hara synthesis, with Vishnu-associated and Shiva-associated worship side by side, similar in spirit to the Lingaraj temple of Bhubaneswar. Legend says a cowherd's cow used to milk over a stone on Bhandar Mountain; the stone oozed blood when stepped on, a priest dreamt of Shiva's instruction, and the local king built the temple. CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the CSV says 'Nayagarh' (the district headquarters), but the temple is at Sarankul, about 13 km from Nayagarh town on the Nayagarh-Aska Road (SH-33), roughly 100 km from Bhubaneswar. It must not be confused with a different Bhubaneswar temple also named 'Ladu Baba' (the old Kainchi/Kainchhi temple in Uttara Daraja, Old Town).

name: Ladubaba Temple
town: Sarankul (CSV town 'Nayagarh' corrected - the temple is at Sarankul, ~13 km from Nayagarh town on the Nayagarh-Aska Road, Nayagarh district)
town_description: Sarankul (Sharanakul) is a town in Nayagarh district, Odisha, about 13 km from the district headquarters Nayagarh on the Nayagarh-Aska Road (SH-33) and roughly 100 km from Bhubaneswar. It is the block headquarters of the Sarankul block and is best known for the Ladubaba (Ladukeswar) Shiva temple, a major pilgrimage centre for Shaivites in southern Odisha.

travel.airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar - about 96 km (per one travel listing, verify).
travel.railway: Nayagarh Town station (Khurda Road-Bolangir line), about 16 km away (per one listing, verify); nearest major railhead is Khurda Road Junction.
travel.road: On the Nayagarh-Odagaon Road (SH-33) at Sarankul; about 13 km from Nayagarh old bus stand; regular buses and shared vehicles from Nayagarh and Bhubaneswar (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: September to February (winter season; per one listing the best months). Mahashivratri (February-March) is the grandest occasion but very crowded.
